template_meta.name: Argosmob SOW Template
template_meta.agency: Argosmob Tech and AI Pvt. Ltd.
template_meta.description: Statement of Work template for web, mobile, and backend projects. Feed project_inputs into AI to generate real values for all placeholder fields.
template_meta.usage: POST /api/v1/utils/generate-sow — pass project_inputs, AI fills all [PLACEHOLDER] fields using this template structure

project_inputs._comment: These are the fields your client/PM fills before calling the AI. AI uses these to generate all section content.
project_inputs.agency_name: Argosmob Tech and AI Pvt. Ltd.

1_1_project_summary.ai_prompt: Write 3 sentences describing what [project_name] is, what problem it solves, who the target users are, and what platforms it consists of. Use project_description and platforms from project_inputs.

rows.ai_prompt: Use client_name if client_entity is empty

1_3_business_objectives.ai_prompt: Generate 5-7 specific, measurable business objectives for [project_name] based on the project_description, key_features, and platforms. Each objective should be one clear sentence starting with an action verb. Make them relevant to a [engagement_model] project for [client_name].

1_4_success_criteria.ai_prompt: Generate 8-12 specific, testable success criteria for [project_name]. Each should be a concrete, verifiable statement (e.g. 'Customer can complete end-to-end checkout on both web and mobile'). Number them SC-01, SC-02 etc. Base them on key_features, platforms, and tech_stack.

section_2.title: Stakeholder Matrix
section_2.ai_prompt: Generate a stakeholder matrix for [project_name]. Use team from project_inputs for names. Generate specific responsibilities and deliverables for each role based on the tech_stack and platforms. Include: Client/Product Owner, Project Manager, UI/UX Designer, Backend Developer, Frontend Developer, Mobile Developer (only if mobile in platforms), DevOps Engineer, QA Engineer.

3_1_frontend_web.ai_prompt: Generate a detailed frontend web tech stack table for [project_name] using tech_stack.frontend as the base framework. Include: Framework (with version), Build Tool, Routing, State Management, HTTP Client, UI Library, Form Handling, Notifications/Toast, Charts (if admin panel), Payment integration method, SEO approach, Code standards. Give specific library names and versions where standard.

3_2_mobile_app.ai_prompt: Generate a detailed mobile app tech stack table for [project_name] using tech_stack.mobile as the base. Include: Framework (with version), Navigation library, State Management, HTTP Client, Payment integration, Push Notifications, Image handling, Storage/cache, Build system, OTA updates. Give specific library names.

3_3_backend.ai_prompt: Generate a detailed backend tech stack table for [project_name] using tech_stack.backend. Include: Runtime (with version), Framework, Architecture pattern, Auth middleware approach, Input validation library, Error handling strategy, Rate limiting, File upload approach, Email provider, Logging libraries, Security libraries, Testing framework. Give specific package names.

3_4_database.ai_prompt: Generate a detailed database tech stack table for [project_name] using tech_stack.database and tech_stack.auth. Include: DB Engine (with version), ORM/Client, Authentication system, File storage, Row Level Security approach, Migration strategy, Seed data approach, Backup strategy, Key database indexes needed.

3_5_payment_gateway.ai_prompt: Generate a payment gateway tech details table for [tech_stack.payment_gateway] used in [project_name]. Include: Product/API used, Supported payment methods (relevant to India), Integration mode, Webhook approach, Sandbox URL, Production URL, API version header, Authentication method.

4_1_high_level.ai_prompt: Write 2-3 paragraphs describing the high-level system architecture for [project_name]. Describe how [platforms] interact with the backend, data access rules, and the overall architectural pattern. Reference specific technologies from tech_stack.

4_2_request_flow.ai_prompt: Generate a step-by-step request flow for [project_name] covering the complete lifecycle from user action to database response and back. Include auth token handling, payment flow hook (if applicable), and webhook handling. Reference specific tech from tech_stack.

4_3_backend_directory.ai_prompt: Generate a realistic, detailed backend directory structure for [project_name] using [tech_stack.backend] with MVC architecture. Include all relevant folders: config, middlewares, routes, controllers, services, schemas, utils. Add inline comments explaining each folder. Name files specifically based on the project's features.

4_4_frontend_directory.ai_prompt: Generate a realistic frontend directory structure for [project_name] using [tech_stack.frontend]. Include: api/, components/ (with sub-folders for feature areas), pages/, store/, hooks/, utils/, constants/. Add inline comments. Organise components based on key_features.

5_1_backend_api.ai_prompt: Generate 15-20 specific backend API scope items for [project_name]. Cover: API versioning, auth middleware, RBAC, input validation, error handling, rate limiting, CORS, pagination standard, soft delete pattern, audit trail, file upload, email notifications, webhook handling, payment integration specifics, search/filter, analytics endpoints. Make items specific to [project_name] features.

5_2_admin_panel.ai_prompt: Generate 12-18 specific admin panel scope items for [project_name]. Cover: protected login, dashboard KPIs, all CRUD management screens relevant to the project, analytics charts, settings screen. List each screen/feature separately with detail.

5_3_frontend_website.ai_prompt: Generate 12-18 specific frontend website scope items for [project_name]. Cover all key pages and features based on key_features. Include header/nav, home page sections, main listing/browsing, detail page, cart/checkout flow, auth, user profile, order history, static pages, responsiveness, loading states.

5_4_mobile_app.ai_prompt: Generate 12-18 specific mobile app scope items for [project_name] using [tech_stack.mobile]. Cover: splash/onboarding, home, listing, detail, cart/checkout, auth screens, profile, push notifications, navigation structure, offline handling. Be specific to the project's features.

5_5_out_of_scope.ai_prompt: Generate a comprehensive out-of-scope list for [project_name] based on out_of_scope from project_inputs plus standard exclusions like: multi-vendor functionality, GPS tracking, loyalty programs, subscription billing, WhatsApp API, third-party logistics, app store submission, content writing, product photography, social media integrations, multi-language/currency support. Include any special_integrations that are explicitly excluded.

section_6.title: Database Schema (All Tables)
section_6.note: All tables include created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now() and updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(). All UUIDs default to gen_random_uuid(). RLS enabled on all tables.
section_6.ai_prompt: Generate a complete, detailed database schema for [project_name] using [tech_stack.database]. Based on the key_features and platforms, design all necessary tables. For each table provide: table name, and for each column: column_name, data_type (PostgreSQL types), constraint (PK/FK/NOT NULL/UNIQUE/DEFAULT/NULLABLE), description. Include all standard tables for the project type plus any project-specific ones. Always include: users/profiles table, core entity tables based on features, junction/relationship tables, settings table, notifications table. Each table should have 8-20 columns as appropriate. Be thorough — missing tables create scope gaps.

section_7.title: API Specification — Complete Reference

header_note.error_format: { success: false, error: { code: 'ERR_CODE', message: '...', details: [...] } }
header_note.auth_legend: Public = no token | Customer = user JWT | Admin = admin-role JWT | Public* = optional auth

section_7.ai_prompt: Generate a complete, production-ready API specification for [project_name]. Group endpoints by resource. For each group generate all CRUD and action endpoints needed. For each endpoint specify: HTTP method, auth level (Public/Customer/Admin), endpoint path (use /api/v1/ prefix, use :id/:slug params), description, request body keys (or query params for GET, or — for none), response keys. Cover ALL resources based on key_features and database schema. Minimum groups: Auth, Users/Profile, [core resource 1], [core resource 2], [more based on features], Orders (if applicable), Payments (if applicable), Reviews (if applicable), Admin Analytics, Notifications, Uploads, Settings. Generate 80-120+ endpoints total. Be thorough — every screen in the frontend needs backing APIs.

section_8.title: Third-Party Integrations
section_8.ai_prompt: Generate detailed integration documentation for all third-party services in [project_name] based on tech_stack and special_integrations. For each integration include: step-by-step flow (8-15 steps), API reference table (sandbox URL, production URL, auth method, webhook approach, key endpoints used), and any important implementation notes. Always cover payment gateway if present, email provider, SMS provider if present, file storage if external, push notification service.

flow.ai_prompt: Generate step-by-step integration flow for [integration_name] in [project_name]

code_example.ai_prompt: Generate a realistic Node.js code example for the key operation of [integration_name] (e.g. create order for payment, send OTP for SMS). Include request setup, response handling, and error case.

9_1_auth_config.ai_prompt: Generate detailed auth configuration table for [project_name] using [tech_stack.auth]. Cover: auth provider, supported methods, token types, access token expiry, refresh token expiry, role storage mechanism, admin vs customer role differentiation, self-hosted vs cloud considerations if applicable.

9_2_storage_buckets.ai_prompt: Generate storage bucket configuration for [project_name] using [tech_stack.storage]. Create appropriate buckets based on the features — e.g. product-images, category-images, avatars, banners, documents. Set realistic max sizes. Public for images, private for sensitive docs.

9_3_rls_policies.ai_prompt: Generate Row Level Security policies for [project_name]'s database tables. For each major table define read, write, and admin policies. Use [tech_stack.auth] JWT claims for role checks. Standard pattern: customers see own data, admins see all, public can read active/published records.

section_10.title: Admin Panel — Detailed Feature Specification
section_10.subsections_ai_prompt: Generate detailed admin panel feature specifications for [project_name]. Create subsections for: Authentication (how admin login works, session management, lockout), Dashboard (exact KPI cards, charts, tables, quick actions), and one subsection per management screen relevant to the project (e.g. Product Management, Order Management, Customer Management, Content Management, etc.). For each screen describe: table/list features, search/filter options, form fields, bulk actions, quick actions. Also include Settings screen with all configurable parameters.

section_11.title: Frontend — Detailed Feature Specification
section_11.subsections_ai_prompt: Generate detailed frontend website feature specifications for [project_name]. Create subsections for: Header & Navigation (layout, mobile behaviour, interactive elements), then one subsection per major page/feature area. For each page describe every section, component, and interactive element in detail. Include a subsection for SEO requirements (meta tags, structured data, sitemap, robots.txt, performance). Cover all pages based on key_features.

12_1_navigation_structure.ai_prompt: Generate the complete React Native navigation tree for [project_name] using React Navigation. Show AuthStack (unauthenticated screens) and AppStack (authenticated, with BottomTabNavigator and nested stacks). Name all screens specifically. Use tree format with └── and ├── characters.

12_2_push_notifications.ai_prompt: Generate all push notification events for [project_name]. Cover every meaningful user action that warrants a push notification based on key_features. Include emojis in titles for engagement.

12_3_offline_error_handling.ai_prompt: Generate offline state and error handling specifications for [project_name] mobile app. Cover: network detection, API error codes handling, token refresh flow, empty states, skeleton screens, retry mechanisms.

13_1_design_tokens.ai_prompt: Generate a complete design token system for [project_name]. Based on the project's industry/type (infer from project_description and project_name), suggest an appropriate colour palette with hex values. Include: Primary Color, Secondary Color, Accent Color, Background (light), Surface/Card, Text Primary, Text Secondary, Border, Success, Warning, Error, Info, Font Display (with name), Font Body (with name), Border Radius (cards), Border Radius (buttons), Border Radius (inputs), Shadow (card), Spacing Scale.

13_2_screen_inventory.ai_prompt: Generate a complete Figma screen inventory for [project_name] with screen IDs (WEB-01, ADM-01, APP-01 etc.) and screen names. Cover all screens for each platform in platforms. Base screen list on key_features and scope of work. Be comprehensive — every user flow needs a screen.

14_1_phase_table.ai_prompt: Generate a 5-phase project timeline for [project_name] using timeline_weeks from project_inputs. For each phase list specific deliverables and what must be ready before the phase can start. Phases: P1 Discovery & Design, P2 Backend Development, P3 Frontend/Admin Panel, P4 Mobile App (if applicable), P5 QA/UAT/Launch.

14_2_payment_schedule.ai_prompt: Generate a milestone payment schedule for [project_name] using payment_schedule from project_inputs. Cover 6 milestones: Kickoff, Design Approval, Backend Complete, Frontend Complete, App Complete, Go-Live. Percentages should sum to 100%.

15_1_server_requirements.ai_prompt: Generate server requirements table for [project_name] using hosting_specs from project_inputs. Include: hosting platform, recommended specs (CPU, RAM, storage), OS, runtime and version, process manager, web server, SSL approach, firewall rules.

15_2_dns_config.ai_prompt: Generate DNS configuration table for [project_name] using domains from project_inputs. Include all subdomains needed for the platforms.

15_3_nginx_config.ai_prompt: Generate a production-ready Nginx configuration for [project_name] covering all domains from project_inputs. Include: HTTP to HTTPS redirect, API reverse proxy to Node.js (with proper headers), static file serving for React builds, cache headers for static assets, client_max_body_size for uploads, SSL certificate paths.

15_4_pm2_config.ai_prompt: Generate a PM2 ecosystem.config.js for [project_name]'s backend. Include cluster mode, memory limit, log paths, env settings. Add comments for common PM2 commands.

15_5_deployment_checklist.ai_prompt: Generate a step-by-step deployment checklist for [project_name] on [hosting_specs.type]. Cover: SSH setup, Node.js install, PM2 install, Nginx install, Certbot install, firewall config, repo clone, dependency install, .env setup, DB migration, frontend build, Nginx vhost config, SSL cert, PM2 start, PM2 auto-start, verification steps, monitoring setup.

16_1_security.ai_prompt: Generate a comprehensive security measures table for [project_name]. Cover: API authentication, HTTPS, security headers, CORS, rate limiting, input validation, SQL/NoSQL injection prevention, file upload security, webhook signature verification, secrets management, dependency auditing. Reference specific packages from tech_stack.

16_2_performance_targets.ai_prompt: Generate realistic performance targets for [project_name]. Cover: page load LCP, API response times (list vs single), mobile Lighthouse score, bundle size, image handling, caching strategy, DB index strategy. Set achievable but professional benchmarks.

17_1_testing_levels.ai_prompt: Generate a testing strategy table for [project_name]. Cover: Unit Tests, Integration Tests, API Tests, E2E Tests, Cross-Browser, Device Testing, Payment Sandbox Testing, Performance Testing, Security Testing, UAT. Reference appropriate tools for [tech_stack.backend] and [tech_stack.frontend].

17_2_critical_test_cases.ai_prompt: Generate 15-20 critical test cases for [project_name] numbered TC-001 onwards. Cover the most important user flows and edge cases based on key_features. Always include: successful happy path flows, failed payment / error cases, auth/role security tests, webhook signature test, rate limit test, stock/inventory edge cases (if applicable), admin vs customer role separation.

18_1_folder_structure.ai_prompt: Generate the Postman collection folder structure for [project_name]. Create numbered folders (00, 01, 02...) matching the API groups from Section 7. For each folder list the specific request names inside it. Include a 00 Health Check folder.

18_2_environment_variables.ai_prompt: Generate Postman environment variables for [project_name]. Include: base_url (staging and prod), auth tokens (auto-set via test scripts), admin token, test user credentials, and dynamic IDs for main resources (auto-set from API responses). Add the test script snippet for auto-setting tokens after login.

19_1_backend_env.ai_prompt: Generate a complete .env file template for [project_name]'s backend using all services in tech_stack. Include sections for: Server config, Database, Auth, Payment Gateway (with all required keys for [tech_stack.payment_gateway]), Email, File Storage, CORS, Rate Limiting, App URLs. Use realistic variable names and placeholder values. Add section comments.

19_2_frontend_env.ai_prompt: Generate the Vite .env file for [project_name]'s frontend (React.js). All vars must be VITE_ prefixed. Include: API URL, app name, app URL, auth service URL and key, payment gateway env flag.

19_3_mobile_env.ai_prompt: Generate the .env / app.config.js variables for [project_name]'s mobile app using [tech_stack.mobile]. Include: API URL, auth config, payment gateway env, Expo project ID, FCM sender ID, deep link scheme.

20_2_app_error_codes.ai_prompt: Generate a complete application error code list for [project_name]. Always include: UNAUTHORIZED (401), FORBIDDEN (403), NOT_FOUND (404), VALIDATION_ERROR (422), DUPLICATE_ENTRY (409), RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (429), WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID (400), PAYMENT_VERIFICATION_FAILED (400), INTERNAL_ERROR (500). Then add project-specific error codes based on key_features (e.g. INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, COUPON_EXPIRED, ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE etc.).

20_3_standard_response_examples.ai_prompt: Generate standard API response format examples for [project_name]: success response (200), created response (201), validation error (422 with field-level details), auth error (401), not found (404), and one project-specific error relevant to the main feature.

21_1_assumptions.ai_prompt: Generate 8-12 project assumptions for [project_name]. Cover: third-party account readiness, content/data delivery by client, brand asset availability, feedback turnaround SLA, payment gateway KYC timeline, app store account requirements, hosting access, any project-specific assumptions based on special_integrations and tech_stack.

21_2_risk_register.ai_prompt: Generate 8-10 project risks for [project_name] numbered R-01 onwards. Always include: client feedback delays, scope creep, third-party service issues, server performance. Add project-specific risks based on tech_stack, special_integrations, and platforms. For each risk give concrete mitigation strategy.

ai_system_prompt._comment: Use this as the system prompt when calling the AI. Paste this into your Express utility.
ai_system_prompt.prompt: You are an expert technical project manager and solution architect at a software agency. Your job is to generate detailed, professional Statement of Work (SOW) documents for software projects. When given project_inputs, you fill in every section of the SOW template with accurate, specific, and detailed content. Rules: 1) Never use vague placeholders like 'Feature X' — always use the actual project name and features. 2) All API endpoints must be real, RESTful, and complete — never skip endpoints that a real project would need. 3) All database tables must be fully designed with real column names, types, and constraints. 4) Tech stack recommendations must reference real package names and versions. 5) Error codes must be specific to the project's domain. 6) Test cases must be specific and testable. 7) Timeline estimates must be realistic for a team of the specified size. 8) All content must be professional, client-ready, and match the quality of a senior technical consultant's work. Output as structured JSON matching the template schema so it can be rendered into a Word document.

express_utility_example._comment: Example Express.js route for your backend utility

code.description: Save this as src/utils/generateSOW.js in your Express backend
code.handler: async (req, res) => { const { project_inputs } = req.body; const template = require('./sow_template.json'); const prompt = buildPrompt(template, project_inputs); const response = await anthropic.messages.create({ model: 'claude-opus-4-5', max_tokens: 8000, system: template.ai_system_prompt.prompt, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }] }); const sow_data = JSON.parse(response.content[0].text); const docxBuffer = await renderSOWtoDocx(sow_data, template); res.setHeader('Content-Disposition', 'attachment; filename=SOW_' + project_inputs.project_name + '.docx'); res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document'); res.send(docxBuffer); }

rendering_hints._comment: Instructions for the docx renderer that converts AI output back into Word format

type_renderers.paragraph: Use P() helper with run() text
type_renderers.bullet_list: Use B() helper for each item
type_renderers.numbered_list: Use N() helper for each item
type_renderers.kv_table: Use kv() helper with rows array
type_renderers.data_table: Use mkTable() helper with headers, widths, rows
type_renderers.api_tables: Use apiSection() helper per group — colour-code methods
type_renderers.code_block: Use codeBlock() helper with Courier New font
type_renderers.signature_table: Use signature table pattern from SOW v2 generator

rendering_hints.section_divider: Use divider() helper at start of each section
rendering_hints.note_box: Use note() for important callouts and warnings
